claims.text: Cu surface segregation governs the onset and progression of the phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu surface segregation creates Cu-rich regions at nanoparticle interfaces.
The Cu-rich regions are locally disordered.
Cu-rich interfacial regions have a lower local melting point.
Cu-rich interfacial regions act as nucleation sites for the overall phase transition.
Heating causes Cu atoms to diffuse toward the nanoparticle surfaces.
Nucleation at Cu-rich surface regions facilitates the propagation of premelting and eventual bulk melting after a critical thermal threshold is reached.
Nanoparticles with pronounced Cu surface segregation will begin melting at a lower temperature than nanoparticles retaining a uniform elemental distribution.
Pronounced Cu surface segregation will produce a spatially heterogeneous onset of melting.
Suppressing Cu segregation will delay melting.
Suppressing Cu segregation will make melting more spatially uniform.
Untreated baseline nanoparticles have a uniform elemental distribution.
Untreated baseline nanoparticles display classical melting behavior with a higher phase-transition onset temperature.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles between 5 and 50 nm under inert atmosphere and controlled heating.
Oxidation and other environmental effects may alter nanoparticle surface chemistry.

contradictions.description: The untreated group is used as the segregation-permitting control and is predicted to melt earlier than the segregation-inhibited coated group, but the baseline field describes untreated nanoparticles as having a higher melting-onset temperature. The reference groups and direction of comparison are therefore inconsistent.
